# Development Tools

[LangChain](https://docs.langchain.com/) = application components
[LangGraph](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/overview) = application logic + orchestration
[LangSmith](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/home) = platform for tracing, observing, evaluating LLM apps

# Control Flow

A **control flow** is the order in which a steps are executed in an LLM app

1. Chain (you decide the path): Input -> Step 1 -> ... -> Step N -> output
2. Agent (LLM decides): Input -> LLM -> ? (tool A / tool B / finish / loop back)

## Chain

A **chain** control flow is linear

- Developer defines sequence of steps
- Steps can include LLM calls

### Examples

**Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)**

- User Question -> Search document store -> put retrieved text into prompt -> LLM writes answer
- Search always happens before the LLM call, even when question doesn't need it

**Document Summarization Pipeline**

- Load PDF -> Split into chunks -> LLM summarize chunks -> LLM combines summaries into 1 summary
- Sequence of steps does not change, regardless of document

**Customer Support Email Triage**

- Receive Email -> LLM extracts structured fields -> Fields saved to DB -> LLM drafts reply
- LLM called twice, but "flow" determines sequence of steps

## Agent

An **agent** control flow is non-linear

- LLM decides the order of steps at runtime
- Developer must define goal and available tools
- LLM repeats a loop until the goal is met
  - Pick an action -> look at result -> pick next action

There are several types of Agents

1. _Router_ = LLM makes one decision and picks one path from defined options
2. _Tool-caller_= LLM repeats reason -> call tool -> look at results until done
3. _Autonomous Multi-agent_ = several specialized agents work together
   a. _Supervisor_ = manager agent hands out tasks to worker agents
   b. _Network (swarm)_ = agents pass work directly to each other
   c. _Hierarchical_ = supervisors manage teams that have their own supervisors
4. _Human-in-the-loop_ = Agent layer; pause control flow for human approval

### Examples

**Customer Support Agent**

- Goal = "My order hasn't arrived. Can you help?"
- Tools = `lookup_order`, `track_shipment`, `issue_refund`, `escalate_to_human`
- Possible sequence of steps
  - LLM -> `lookup_order(customer_id)` -> order #881, shipped 10 days ago
  - LLM -> `track_shipment(#881)` -> "lost in transit"
  - LLM -> `issue_refund(#881)` -> refund approved
  - LLM -> reply: "Your package was lost. We've issued a full refund"
  - Stops

**Research Assistant**

- Goal = "Compare the populations of the capitals of France and Japan"
- Tools = `web_search`, `read_webpage`
- Possible sequence of steps
  - LLM -> `web_search("capital of Japan")` -> Tokyo
  - LLM -> `web_search("population of Paris")` -> ~2.1 million
  - LLM -> `web_search("population of Tokyo")` -> results unclear
  - LLM -> `read_webpage(tokyo_gov_stats_url)` -> ~14 million (city)
  - LLM -> reply with comparison
  - Stops

# Foundational Concepts

## How LLMs Work

- _Chat models_ = LLM takes list of messages -> returns new message
  - Models do not remember past calls
  - Must recent conversation history for each call
  - Possible to persist "state" of conversation

- _Message Roles_
  - System = instructions for the LLM
  - Human = what the user says
  - AI = LLM's replies
  - Tools = the results of tool calls

- _Tokens_ = small pieces of text that is read by LLM
- _Context Window_ = size of text model can read at once
  - Long conversations must be trimmed or compressed

- _Tool-calling_ = LLM only asks for a tool to be run (tool + inputs)
  - Code runs the tool and sends back results

- _Structured-output_ = LLM to reply in a fixed format (eg. JSON)
  - Router control flows rely on structured output to make clear decisions

## LangChain Concepts

- _Chat-Model Classes_ = one shared interface (eg. `ChatOpenAI`)
  - Possible to switch LLM providers without re-writing code

- _Message Classes_ = Python objedts for each message role
  - Examples: `HumanMessage`, `AIMessage`, `SystemMessage`, `ToolMessage`

- _Tools_ = ordinary python functions
  - Docstring and type hints tell LLM what tool does and how to use
  - `bind_tools()` tells LLM which tools it is allowed to request

- `.invoke()` or `.stream()` = standard way to run LLM model or graph
  - Invoke to return full result at end of control flow
  - Stream to return results piece by piece as it is produced

## LangGraph Concepts

- _State_ = shared `TypedDict` record that every node reads/writes
- _Node_ = python function that does one job
  - Examples: call LLM, run tool, return updates to state
- _Edge_ = fixed connection between nodes
  - Conditional edge = function looks at state; chooses which node to run next
- _START / END_ = makers defining where graph begins and where it stops
- _Reducer_ = rule for updating state; replace old value or append to list
- `builder.compile()` = checks structure, converts to something you can run
- _Checkpointer_ = saves state after every step; provides memory across calls
